data.long_meaning: Derived from the Persian word 'Khorshid', meaning 'Sun'. In Hinduism, the name Khursid is associated with the sun god, Surya, and represents radiance, power, and energy. Linguistically it belongs to the Persian tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Khursid usually hope their child will grow to embody sun, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Khursid holds cultural significance in Hinduism due to its Persian origin connecting it to the sun god Surya, who is highly revered in Hindu culture and mythology. Khursid may have been adopted by Hindus as a personal name to embody the sun's energy and power.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Khursid lies in its connection to the celestial body of the sun and the Hindu deity Surya, who represents the source of all life, energy, and power. It is believed that the name resonates with the divine energy of the sun and fosters qualities such as creativity, courage, and strength within the person bearing it.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Khursid is believed to have originated from the Persian word 'Khorshid', meaning 'Sun'. In Hindu culture, the Sun represents knowledge, power, and illumination. Therefore, the name Khursid symbolizes the inner radiance and enlightenment of an individual.

historical_references.context: Khursid was the eldest son of Zahiruddin Muhammad Babur and succeeded his father upon his death.
